answer.rationale: Memory 44 most directly supports qualified-revenue potential through higher-quality enterprise pipeline, though it omits closed-won, retention, and unit-economics outcomes. Memory 57 reports qualified revenue and no measurable retention harm, but is limited to established customers and omits longer-term LTV and incentive cost. Memory 73 reports acquisition and revenue lift for price-sensitive SMBs, but omits retention, margin, and whether promotional pricing creates durable revenue. Memories 31, 86, and 91 support upstream activation/adoption indicators rather than qualified revenue; memory 91 is least supported because it reports only week-one engagement and first meaningful action, with no revenue, qualification, retention, or durability evidence.
